sources.title: Daugava Museum: Daugavas lībieši vēlajā dzelzs laikmetā
sources.note: Tenth-century lower Daugava Livonian settlement; Finnic identity and contacts with Baltic and Scandinavian cultures.

sources.title: Latvian State Inspection for Heritage Protection: Grobiņa archaeological ensemble
sources.note: Tentative-list submission, description and Priediens burial ground: seventh to ninth-century Curonian and Scandinavian interaction, jewelry with Baltic influences. Not a World Heritage inscription claim.

sources.title: Guntis Zemītis: Ornament and symbol at Āraiši Lake Castle
sources.note: 2023 research abstract, ninth/tenth-century Latgalian settlement, waterlogged structures, wooden bowls and blanks, bast shoes and beekeeping tools.

sources.title: Āraiši Ezerpils Archaeological Park: the lake settlement
sources.note: Museum description: ninth/tenth-century settlement, subsistence activities, reconstructed buildings based on excavated structural details. Modern educational recipes excluded.

sources.title: Šarūnė Valotkienė and Vikinta Černeckytė: Combs from the third to twelfth centuries in Lithuania
sources.note: English summary printed 176 to178; Kretuonys barrow52 composite double-sided comb, dated ninth century to early second millennium. Original indexed PDF text; direct PDF fetch failed.

sources.title: Latvian National Intangible Cultural Heritage List: Tablet weaving in Northern Latgale
sources.note: History section: sixth-century band fragments and elaborate eleventh/thirteenth-century Latgalian and Livonian examples. Modern cradle uses and teaching practices not projected into early medieval period.

sources.title: Laurynas Kurila: The status of children in Iron Age East Lithuania
sources.note: 2007 study, archaeological burial changes in eighth to eleventh/twelfth centuries. Do not repeat speculative claims that parents felt less affection or infer gender reliably from grave goods.

sources.title: Šiauliai Tourism Information Centre, Balts’ Road: The Baltic Art
sources.note: Institutional educational synthesis based on Art of the Balts exhibition catalogue2009; Amber amulets section, seventh/ninth-century Lazdininkai and Palanga comb-shaped pendants. Folklore explanation not treated as established prehistoric meaning.

sources.title: Jos Schaeken: Observations on the Old Prussian Basel Epigram
sources.note: Printed331to332, oldest extant Baltic text, adjacent1369 colophon, Kayle rekyse and Hello,mister translation. Existing prussians card also uses this URL; include its public words in combined budget.
